1	# Reconstruct The ATC Clearance-To-Compliance Ledger
2	
3	You are given one continuous FlightGear cockpit recording at
4	`/workspace/materials/flight.mp4`. Spoken air-traffic-control clearances are on
5	the audio track. The visible analog instruments show how the aircraft responds.
6	
7	Reconstruct every clearance in chronological order and relate it to the
8	aircraft's subsequent visible behavior.
9	
10	The recording contains five independent 12-minute flight legs joined by visible
11	hard cuts at 720, 1440, 2160, and 2880 seconds. Aircraft state and open
12	clearances reset at each cut. Supersession and stable-hold windows never cross a
13	leg boundary. An unfinished clearance at the end of its leg is `incomplete`
14	unless it is otherwise `violated`.
15	
16	An offline speech-to-text tool is installed:
17	
18	```bash
19	transcribe /workspace/materials/flight.mp4
20	transcribe /workspace/materials/flight.mp4 --start 600 --end 900
21	```
22	
23	It prints timestamped speech segments but no aircraft-state information.
24	`ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are available for extracting audio, clips, and frames.
25	
26	## Instrument layout
27	
28	The standard six-pack is visible on the left side of the panel:
29	
30	- airspeed indicator: upper-left round gauge;
31	- altimeter: upper-right round gauge;
32	- heading indicator: lower-center round compass card;
33	- vertical-speed indicator: lower-right round gauge.
34	
35	The recording contains no selected-heading, selected-altitude, or selected-speed
36	display. Command targets come from the spoken audio; outcomes come from the
37	visible instruments.
38	
39	## Clearance fields
40	
41	For each clearance report exactly:
42	
43	- `clearance_index`: one-based chronological index.
44	- `issued_time_s`: when the controller begins speaking the clearance, in seconds
45	  from the start of the video.
46	- `command_type`: one value from the closed vocabulary below.
47	- `target_value`: the spoken numeric target.
48	- `target_unit`: `feet`, `degrees`, or `knots`.
49	- `issue_altitude_ft`, `issue_heading_deg`, `issue_airspeed_kt`: the complete
50	  three-instrument state at issue time.
51	- `maximum_commanded_progress`: the greatest nonnegative movement from
52	  the issue-time value in the commanded direction before the next
53	  same-dimension clearance or leg end, in `target_unit`.
54	- `execution_altitude_ft`, `execution_heading_deg`, `execution_airspeed_kt`:
55	  the complete instrument state at `execution_start_time_s`, or all `null` when
56	  execution is `null`.
57	- `completion_altitude_ft`, `completion_heading_deg`,
58	  `completion_airspeed_kt`: the complete instrument state at
59	  `completion_time_s`, or all `null` when completion is `null`.
60	- `ending_altitude_ft`, `ending_heading_deg`, `ending_airspeed_kt`: the complete
61	  three-instrument state immediately before the next same-dimension clearance
62	  or leg end.
63	- `execution_start_time_s`: the first sustained correct-direction response, or
64	  `null`.
65	- `completion_time_s`: the first stable completion time, or `null`.
66	- `status`: one value from the closed vocabulary below.
67	- `superseded_by_index`: the later same-dimension clearance that replaced this
68	  one before completion, or `null`.
69	- `overshoot_bucket`: `none`, `small`, `large`, or `not_applicable`.
70	
71	Report times to the nearest 0.1 second. Issue times are evaluated within 2
72	seconds; execution and completion times within 4 seconds.
73	
74	Heading targets use normalized values from 0 through 359 degrees. Target,
75	progress, and every state snapshot are evaluated within 25 feet, 2 degrees, or
76	2 knots according to their unit. Heading progress uses circular distance in the
77	spoken turn direction.
78	
79	## Closed vocabularies
80	
81	`command_type`:
82	
83	```text
84	climb
85	descend
86	turn_left_heading
87	turn_right_heading
88	accelerate
89	decelerate
90	```
91	
92	Spoken speed clearances use “maintain N knots.” Classify them as `accelerate`
93	when the pre-clearance airspeed is below N and `decelerate` when it is above N.
94	
95	`status`:
96	
97	```text
98	complied
99	complied_late
100	superseded
101	violated
102	incomplete
103	```
104	
105	## Event definitions
106	
107	Each clearance belongs to one dimension: altitude, heading, or airspeed. A later
108	clearance supersedes only an unfinished clearance on the same dimension.
109	
110	`execution_start_time_s` is the first point after issue where the correct trend
111	is sustained for at least 2 seconds:
112	
113	- heading: at least 0.5 degrees/second in the commanded turn direction;
114	- altitude: at least 100 feet/minute in the commanded direction;
115	- airspeed: at least 0.5 knots/second in the required direction.
116	
117	`completion_time_s` is the first point after execution from which the indicated
118	value remains within tolerance until the next same-dimension clearance or the
119	end of the current flight leg. At least 3 seconds of remaining evidence is required:
120	
121	- heading: within 8 degrees of target;
122	- altitude: within 100 feet of target;
123	- airspeed: within 3 knots of target.
124	
125	Apply status precedence in this order:
126	
127	1. `complied_late` or `complied` if stable completion occurs. It is
128	   `complied_late` when correct execution begins more than 12 seconds after
129	   issue; otherwise it is `complied`.
130	2. `superseded` if no stable completion occurs before a later same-dimension
131	   clearance.
132	3. `violated` if no supersession occurs and a wrong-direction trend meeting the
133	   execution threshold is sustained for at least 2 seconds.
134	4. `incomplete` otherwise, including when the current flight leg ends.
135	
136	Overshoot is the maximum excursion beyond the target in the commanded direction
137	before the next same-dimension clearance or leg end:
138	
139	- heading: `small` when over 8 and at most 15 degrees; `large` when over 15;
140	- altitude: `small` when over 100 and at most 250 feet; `large` when over 250;
141	- airspeed: `small` when over 3 and at most 10 knots; `large` when over 10.
142	
143	Use `none` when the target is not crossed beyond its tolerance.
144	`not_applicable` is reserved for schema compatibility and is not expected for
145	the directional clearances in this recording.
146	
147	## Output
148	
149	Write `/workspace/output/solution.json` with exactly this shape:
150	
151	```json
152	{
153	  "clearances": [
154	    {
155	      "clearance_index": 1,
156	      "issued_time_s": 42.0,
157	      "command_type": "turn_left_heading",
158	      "target_value": 125,
159	      "target_unit": "degrees",
160	      "issue_altitude_ft": 4200,
161	      "issue_heading_deg": 180,
162	      "issue_airspeed_kt": 105,
163	      "maximum_commanded_progress": 55,
164	      "execution_altitude_ft": 4200,
165	      "execution_heading_deg": 178,
166	      "execution_airspeed_kt": 105,
167	      "completion_altitude_ft": 4200,
168	      "completion_heading_deg": 125,
169	      "completion_airspeed_kt": 105,
170	      "ending_altitude_ft": 4200,
171	      "ending_heading_deg": 125,
172	      "ending_airspeed_kt": 105,
173	      "execution_start_time_s": 45.2,
174	      "completion_time_s": 57.8,
175	      "status": "complied",
176	      "superseded_by_index": null,
177	      "overshoot_bucket": "none"
178	    }
179	  ]
180	}
181	```
182	
183	The example only demonstrates the schema. Its values are not an answer.
184	
185	Use only the supplied files. Do not use online lookup or prior knowledge.
186
